title: Reclaim Your Focus: Discover Time Tracker - The Ultimate Web Habit Builder!
article:
Hey fellow developers! Ever find yourself diving into a rabbit hole of tabs, only to emerge hours later wondering where your time went? We've all been there. The internet is an incredible resource, but it can also be a massive distraction. What if there was a super cool, open-source project that could help you understand your browsing habits and actually build better ones? Well, get ready to say 'Wow, I need to check this out!' because I've stumbled upon Time Tracker - Web Habit Builder, and it's a game-changer.

Time Tracker is a powerful browser extension available for Chrome, Firefox, and Edge that does exactly what its name suggests: it tracks the time you spend on websites. But it's so much more than a simple timer. This project is designed to give you deep insights into your digital life and empower you to take control. Imagine having detailed browsing records, intuitive dashboards, and analytical reports that clearly show you where your precious time is going. No more guessing games!

What truly makes this project stand out is its comprehensive feature set. Beyond just tracking, it allows for sophisticated website management. You can set up whitelist and merge rules to categorize your sites effectively. Feeling distracted? Time Tracker lets you set daily, weekly, or even per-visit limits for specific websites, and here's the best part: it can even block pages when those limits are reached. This isn't just passive tracking; it's active habit building! Plus, for those dedicated work sessions, it includes built-in Focus and Pomodoro sessions to keep you on task.

For developers, the benefits are clear. Not only can this tool drastically improve your personal productivity by minimizing distractions and fostering healthier online habits, but the project itself is built with a modern tech stack including Rspack, TypeScript, Vue 3, Element Plus, and ECharts. This means it's a fantastic resource for learning and even contributing to an active, useful open-source project. And let's not forget the robust data management features: you can synchronize data across browsers, back up your data to GitHub Gist, WebDAV, or even Obsidian Local REST API, ensuring your insights are always safe and accessible. It’s a complete package for anyone looking to optimize their digital workflow and regain focus. Seriously, go give it a star on GitHub and try it out!
key_takeaways: Time Tracker is a cross-browser extension for tracking website usage and building better digital habits.
It offers detailed analytics, dashboards, and reports to help users understand their online time allocation.
Key features include website limits, page blocking, and integrated Focus/Pomodoro sessions for active habit improvement.
The project supports data synchronization and robust backup options (Gist, WebDAV, Obsidian) for data security.
Built with a modern tech stack (Vue 3, TypeScript), it's a great open-source project for both users and contributors.
readme_summary: Time Tracker - Web Habit Builder is a browser extension designed to help users understand and manage their online habits. It provides detailed tracking of website usage, analytical reports, website blocking, and focus tools like Pomodoro sessions, with cross-browser compatibility and data synchronization/backup options.
description: A browser extension that helps you track time, analyze your habits and block addictive sites
